public.prompt: A legacy application has many `innerHTML` sinks. The security team wants supporting browsers to reject raw strings at injection sinks and permit HTML only through one named sanitizing policy. Which rollout contract enforces both boundaries?

options.label: Create an unrestricted default policy that returns every input unchanged, without adding a Trusted Types CSP.
Require Trusted Types for script sinks, allowlist one policy name, and make that policy sanitize before creating HTML.
Allowlist one policy name in CSP, keep passing strings to sinks, and sanitize only after assignment failures occur.

answerProof.summary: The require-trusted-types-for directive blocks string assignment to covered sinks, while trusted-types restricts policy creation; the allowed policy still needs a real sanitizer.
decisiveConstraints: Raw strings must be rejected at covered injection sinks.
Only one expected policy name may be created.
Policy output must be sanitized rather than merely retyped.

claims.statement: The require-trusted-types-for CSP directive makes covered injection sinks reject strings, while the trusted-types directive restricts which policy names may be created.
Trusted Types policy code is application-defined and must perform the intended sanitization before creating TrustedHTML.

optionRationales.explanation: Without enforcement, strings remain accepted, and a pass-through default policy converts unsafe input without sanitizing it.
optionRationales.plausibility: A default policy can ease migration by adapting legacy string assignments in one central location.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The browser must reject uncovered raw strings and policy output must remove unsafe markup.

optionRationales.explanation: The two CSP directives enforce typed sink input and policy naming, while the named policy owns sanitization.
Policy allowlisting alone does not require callers to use Trusted Types at injection sinks.
optionRationales.plausibility: Restricting policy names reduces the chance that arbitrary code creates a permissive policy.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Raw string assignment must fail before unsafe content reaches a covered sink.
